entries.abstract: An unconditional Lean formalization of Theorem 1.2 of arXiv:2608.26062v2: a real meromorphic function has three infinite exceptional fibres on the real axis, while every other point divisor fails the Blaschke condition in each half-plane and the function is not of bounded type in either.
entries.title: Three omitted values and non-Blaschke point divisors in half-planes

entries.abstract: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p.
entries.title: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number

entries.abstract: This entry formalizes the Ewens sampling formula for partitions of n and its relation to a generative urn. Over any field of characteristic zero, the weights sum to 1 whenever the rising factorial in θ is nonzero, and they have an explicit product form in the part counts. For θ > 0 the urn law on partitions of n equals the Ewens weights. The conditional law given the number of parts is expressed through Stirling numbers of the first kind, and the weights are consistent under deletion of one sampled individual.
entries.title: The Ewens sampling formula and its generative urn

entries.abstract: This entry formalizes degree and divisibility facts about the denominators of solutions to the two-locus sampling recursion with two alleles at each locus. Centred moments of a solution, grouped in blocks by the numbers i and j of lineages at the two loci, satisfy a tridiagonal linear system with matrix T(i, j) whose right-hand side involves only smaller blocks. An explicit product D of linear factors in the mutation rates and of block determinants E(p, s) = det T(p, s) clears the denominator of the solution: D times the solution lies in any subring that contains the parameters. Conditionally on D being the reduced denominator of the top centred moment, every denominator of the solution is divisible by E. The determinant E(i, j) has degree min(i, j) in the recombination rate when a nonvanishing condition holds, and is positive when i, j ≥ 2 and the rates are nonnegative. Two statements show that the diagonal determinants E(m, m), with one mutation rate set to zero, have irreducible factors of unbounded degree as m varies, both as polynomials in the mutation rate over rational functions of the recombination rate and as polynomials in the recombination rate over rational functions of the mutation rate.
entries.title: An upper bound on the denominators of solutions of the two-locus sampling recursion

entries.abstract: This entry formalizes a prespecified fixed-sample test, based on independent blocks of three linked sites observed at three sampled tips with four allelic states, of a panmictic null model against a two-deme alternative. Under the null, the three-tip genealogy follows the coalescent with a time-varying pair-coalescence rate r, and sites mutate under the four-state equal-rates model with scale k. For every nonnegative locally integrable rate r whose integrated clock diverges and every k > 0, the rejection probability with at least 72,000,000,000 independent blocks is at most 1/20. For one specific two-island alternative, with all three tips sampled in the same deme, the rejection probability is at least 4/5 with exactly 72,000,000,000 blocks and at least 19/20 with exactly 250,000,000,000 blocks. The test, its features, its betting factors, its localization tolerance, and its threshold are fixed numerical choices given in the Challenge.
entries.title: A prespecified betting test of panmixia against a two-deme history: size and power

entries.abstract: This entry states correctness results, in exact rational arithmetic, for an executable implementation of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination under parent-independent mutation, with two alleles at each locus. For valid parameters and configurations with the stated array sizes, the computation succeeds and its value equals the solution of the recursion at the decoded configuration. A table checker is shown to be sound and complete: a table that passes the check consists of true values of the recursion, and the table of true values over the closure of configurations of a given size passes. The existence of a solution to the recursion, for any finite numbers of alleles, positive mutation rates, and nonnegative recombination rate, is also stated, together with an explicit characterization of the Boolean parameter-validity test.
entries.title: A kernel-checked implementation of the biallelic two-locus sampling recursion, and a table checker

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main result of the author's preprint "Affine Profile Reduction for Fractional Triangle Packings in Split Graphs" (Erdős #81 series, Paper I): for every finite split graph G on n vertices, |E(G)| − 2ν₃*(G) ≤ n²/6 + n/2, where ν₃* is the fractional triangle packing number (the maximum total weight of a nonnegative weighting of the triangles with load at most one on every edge). It is stated both for the paper's finite split model (clique Fin p, independent vertices, neighbourhoods) and for every split graph in Mathlib's SimpleGraph, with the definitions of split graphs and fractional triangle packings of two registered entries; the weaker bound n²/6 + n of the first edition is also included. The proof reduces the fractional packing problem to neighbourhood profiles and a three-variable linear program, using finite LP duality. Version 2 states the finite LP duality used in the series as results of its own, over ℝ (Farkas' lemma in inequality form and covering/packing strong duality, from this proof) and over ℚ (Farkas' lemma by Fourier–Motzkin elimination and strong duality for the rational packing LP, from the author's Paper V).
entries.title: Affine profile reduction for fractional triangle packings in split graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Galvin’s theorem for finite bipartite multigraphs: every assignment of finite edge lists of size at least the maximum incidence degree admits a proper edge coloring, with parallel edges counted separately. It includes ordinary edge coloring with Δ colors and the matching lower bound, and the Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall theorem for local lists (lists of size at least the larger degree of the two ends of each edge suffice). The previously registered simple-graph Galvin theorem, Dinitz problem and Gale–Shapley stable matching theorem are retained.
entries.title: Galvin's theorem for bipartite multigraphs, the Dinitz problem and stable matchings

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Moser–Tardos theorem in the variable setting: finitely many independent random variables with finite ranges, n events each determined by a finite set of variables, neighbours sharing a variable. If P(A_j) ≤ x_j ∏_{k ∈ Γ(j)} (1 − x_k) with 0 ≤ x_j < 1, the resampling algorithm (always resampling the first violated event), run on a random resampling table, resamples A_j at most x_j / (1 − x_j) times in expectation among its first t steps, for every t; the expected total number of resamplings is at most ∑_j x_j / (1 − x_j); the probability that it has not stopped after t steps is at most (∑_j x_j / (1 − x_j)) / t; and some assignment avoids all events (the Lovász Local Lemma in the variable setting). The proof formalizes witness trees built from the log, the τ-check coupling with the resampling table, and the Galton–Watson bound.
entries.title: The Moser–Tardos theorem (algorithmic Lovász Local Lemma)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Corrádi–Hajnal theorem (1963): every finite simple graph on at least 3k vertices with minimum degree at least 2k contains k vertex-disjoint cycles. Cycles are closed walks that are cycles in Mathlib's sense; the theorem is also stated with the definition of disjoint cycles of the registered Erdős–Pósa entry (k pairwise disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a subgraph that is not acyclic). Both hypotheses are shown to be needed: for k ≥ 2 the complete graph on 3k − 1 vertices has minimum degree 3k − 2 ≥ 2k and no k disjoint cycles, and for m ≥ 2k the complete bipartite graph K_{2k−1, m} has at least 3k vertices and minimum degree 2k − 1 and no k disjoint cycles. Mathlib has cycles and minimum degree but not this theorem.
entries.title: The Corrádi–Hajnal theorem on vertex-disjoint cycles

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing" (Erdős #81 series, Paper III): there is an absolute constant C such that every finite split graph G on n vertices satisfies |E(G)| − 2ν₃(G) ≤ n²/6 + C·n, where ν₃(G) is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles (Theorem 1.1); consequently G has a clique partition (a family of cliques covering every edge exactly once) with at most n²/6 + C·n cliques (Corollary 1.2). The quadratic coefficient 1/6 is the sharp one for split graphs. The constant C is existential and not explicit. Two ingredients of the proof, the asymptotic gap between fractional and integral triangle packings and exact triangle decompositions of dense triangle-divisible graphs, are taken from two registered formalizations (see related_formalizations).
entries.title: Linear-error clique partitions of split graphs

entries.abstract: One assembled Lean formalization of principal refined absorption results and their consequences. The selected results include refined omni-absorbers and refiners, labelled reserve matchings, dense compatible decompositions, an additive compatible-absorber interface retaining independence of the entire old ambient vertex set, and existence of simple designs for every fixed q > r ≥ 2 and index λ ≥ 1 at all sufficiently large admissible orders. The literal global embedding conclusion of the survey is refuted separately from a proved piecewise replacement. The research-note endpoints give completion avoiding an arbitrary forbidden partial Steiner system, sparse prescribed and finite embedded exact intersections, an initial polynomial intersection interval, and polynomial excess in partial parallel classes and Nash–Williams schedule rounds. Both external inputs are supplied by pinned proved theorems. The single comparison selects eighteen declarations from the existing aggregate proof root.
entries.title: Formalizing Delcourt–Postle’s refined absorption in Lean

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main result of the author's preprint "Complete-Split Extremizers for a Fractional Triangle-Cover Functional on Chordal Graphs" (Erdős #81 series, Paper II). For a finite simple graph G let τ₃*(G) be its fractional triangle cover number (the least total weight of a nonnegative weighting of vertex pairs giving every triangle weight at least one on its edges) and Φ_τ(G) = |E(G)| − 2τ₃*(G). For every n ≥ 1, every chordal graph on n vertices satisfies Φ_τ(G) ≤ ⌊(2n + 1)²/24⌋, and equality is attained by a complete-split graph K_p ∨ K̄_q with p + q = n (Theorem 1.2). Chordality and fractional triangle covers use the definitions of two registered entries.
entries.title: Complete-split extremizers for the fractional triangle-cover deficit on chordal graphs

entries.abstract: This entry formalizes an identifiability theorem for three sampled sequences whose sites all share one random three-tip genealogy (complete linkage). A genealogy is a pair of branch lengths (u, v), where u is the height of the cherry and v is the length of the upper internal branch, together with a label in Fin 3 recording which pair of tips forms the cherry. Its law is an arbitrary finite measure that is almost everywhere supported on nonnegative branch lengths. Given the genealogy, sites evolve independently under the K-state equal-rates mutation model with a uniform root distribution and mutation scale k. For K ≥ 2 and k, l ≥ 0, two such measures, with scales k and l, produce the same law of block patterns for every number L of linked sites if and only if their collapsed objects agree. The collapsed object is the push-forward of the measure under (u, v, q) ↦ (k u, k v, q), with the cherry label replaced by a fixed value whenever k v = 0. A second statement shows that, for a genealogy with zero upper branch (a star tree), the block-pattern law does not depend on which cherry label is attached.
entries.title: Linked-site block laws of all lengths identify the collapsed mutation-scaled genealogy

entries.abstract: Three continuous counterexamples in uniform polynomial approximation: a nonodd function whose best approximants all vanish at zero, a nonodd function with plateaus at degrees (2k+1,2k+2), and a noneven function with plateaus at degrees (2k,2k+1). Exact algebraic certificates, analytic contact persistence, and cubic self-similarity prove all three results. This repository contains the substantive formalization and formalizes the owner-supplied mathematical manuscripts.
entries.title: Self-similar counterexamples to three conjectures of Lorentz

entries.abstract: For a continuous weakly mixing self-map of a nonempty Polish space, a comeagre set of countable sequences has every finite prefix dense under the corresponding diagonal forward orbit. A nonempty dense G-delta subset of such sequences is constructed through countable-product transitivity and a countable-basis Baire argument.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Generic strongly transitive sequences in weakly mixing Polish systems

entries.abstract: For a continuous self-map of a nonempty topological space, square transitivity implies transitivity of every finite diagonal power, including power zero. A genuine open-pair refinement and finite induction give a common natural forward hitting time for any finite family of nonempty open pairs. The literal two-pair condition is proved equivalent to actual square transitivity.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Furstenberg weak mixing and finite diagonal powers

entries.abstract: Eventual equality on the actual Cantor product has a BP invariant-set zero-one law. Every invariant map with BP open preimages into a second countable T0 target has a comeagre constant fiber. Consequently no such BP map, and no Borel map with explicit Borel sigma-algebras, reduces eventual equality to equality.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Generic ergodicity and non-smoothness of E₀

entries.abstract: A formal proof that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between arbitrary complex unital C*-algebras is an algebraic Jordan isomorphism. The development also proves that a bounded generator whose exponentials are unital spectral isometries at every complex parameter is an associative derivation, and that every surjective spectral isometry is a unital Jordan isomorphism multiplied by its prescribed central unitary value at the identity.
entries.title: A proof of the spectral isometry conjecture for C*-algebras

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked transfer of the exact CHSH constants for self-adjoint involutions (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple in a C*-normed ring: the norm of the CHSH operator T = A0 B0 + A0 B1 + A1 B0 - A1 B1 is at most 2*sqrt(2), equals 2 under a commuting party (the equality in a nontrivial real C*-normed algebra; the <= forms in every C*-normed ring), and exceeds 2 only if both parties are noncommuting) to self-adjoint CONTRACTIONS, together with the state corollary. A CHSH contraction tuple is four self-adjoint operators of norm at most 1 with the four cross-party commutations - IsCHSHTuple with the involution relations relaxed to norm bounds. The route is the Halmos dilation A -> A (x) Z + sqrt(1 - A^2) (x) X (Halmos 1950), applied with ONE ANCILLA PER OBSERVABLE: the four dilations form a Mathlib IsCHSHTuple on n (x) (C^2)^(x)4, every commutation relation among the four observables transfers to the dilations, the dilated CHSH operator compresses to T, and compression does not increase the operator norm, so every involution bound transfers. One ancilla per party would not do: for B0 = 1, B1 = 0 the single-ancilla dilations 1 (x) Z and 1 (x) X anticommute, so the commuting-party bound would not transfer. Nine compared statements: for n x n complex matrices (l2-operator norm), norm T <= 2*sqrt(2), norm T <= 2 if either party commutes, and 2 < norm T forces both parties noncommuting; for every density matrix rho, (1/2)|Re tr(rho T)| <= sqrt(2), and <= 1 under a commuting party; the same three norm bounds for bounded operators on a complete complex inner-product space (ampliation on the Hilbert sum WithLp 2 (E x E)); and, RESTATED, the parallelogram bound norm(A0 (B0 + B1) + A1 (B0 - B1)) <= 2*sqrt(2) for four operators of norm at most 1 with no self-adjointness and no commutation (folklore; formalized in Lean by Physical Superintelligence, 2026-10-23; proved independently here). The involution constants are the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000007, re-proved here as library support and not compared. The bounds themselves are classical (Tsirelson 1980; the commuting-algebra bound as used by Summers and Werner 1987); new in this entry, relative to the Lean prior art recorded under sources (PSI's parallelogram and Hilbert-space state bounds; Lean-QIT's Kronecker-form state bound for contractions), are the contraction statements in the forms stated and their derivation from the involution constants by dilation (statements 1 and 6 are, as statements, the self-adjoint cross-commuting case of the parallelogram bound; their novelty is the route). The Challenge imports Mathlib only; the three structures it uses (IsCHSHContractionTuple for matrices, IsDensityMatrix, Hilbert.IsCHSHContractionTuple for operators) are verbatim copies of the library's, checked byte for byte by scripts/check_challenge_definitions.py. The Mathlib definitions the statements import (the scoped l2-operator norm on matrices, PosSemidef under ComplexOrder, IsSelfAdjoint and the adjoint, the trace, the operator norm, WithLp 2, IsCHSHTuple) are quoted verbatim from the pinned source with permalinks in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md and kernel-checked in DefinitionAudit.lean, a default build target that is not compared.
entries.title: CHSH bounds for contractions by dilation: Tsirelson's bound, the classical bound under a commuting party, and the necessity of noncommutativity

entries.abstract: For any topological source and second countable target, open inverse images have the property of Baire exactly when the function restricts continuously to some comeagre G-delta subspace. A Baire-source corollary also proves density. The countable basis synchronization and converse relative-open argument are proved internally.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Baire-measurable regularization on comeagre G-delta subspaces

entries.abstract: A homomorphism from a Baire topological group to a separable topological group is continuous if every open inverse image has the property of Baire. The neighborhood lemma for nonmeagre BP sets and the countable right-translate cover are proved internally. No separation, source-Polish, injectivity or surjectivity hypothesis.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Pettis automatic continuity for Baire-to-separable topological groups

entries.abstract: CONDITIONAL on two cited results, both taken as explicit hypotheses of the theorems and never as axioms: PPS1984Remark, the printed Remark on p. 530 of A. Perelli, J. Pintz and S. Salerno, Bombieri's theorem in short intervals, 1984, and PP1993Goldbach, the Goldbach analogue of Theorem 3 of A. Perelli and J. Pintz, On the exceptional set for Goldbach's problem in short intervals, 1993, established in its sections 3 to 5 but not printed as a numbered theorem. These are the inputs that the paper's own proof quotes as its Theorems 2.1 and 2.3. PP1993Goldbach is therefore a weaker citation than a numbered theorem: it is the unnumbered Goldbach analogue that Halupczok says the proof of Perelli and Pintz can be adapted to give, stated here in the general form that argument yields. Under the two hypotheses, a complete Lean 4 proof of a repaired form of Theorem 1.2 of K. Halupczok, Goldbach's problem with primes in arithmetic progressions and in short intervals, J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 25, 2013, 331 to 351: summed over moduli q <= Q, the weighted count of p1 + p2 + p3 = n with p1 = a mod q and p1, p2 in short intervals differs from its singular series main term T(n, q, a) Y1 Y2 by << Y1 Y2 L^-A. As printed, the theorem sums over all q <= Q with the printed T, which does not vanish when a and q have a common factor, while the prime sum then is empty, so the printed statement fails, for example at a = 3, q = 3. The repair takes the main term to be 0 for such q, or equivalently restricts to q coprime to a. The entry also proves that the two hypotheses imply the paper's Theorems 2.1 and 2.3, as derived results of this entry. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; ternary Goldbach is a theorem of Helfgott. An AI agent wrote the Lean code; the statements were checked against the sources by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: CONDITIONAL on Perelli-Pintz-Salerno 1984 and Perelli-Pintz 1993: Halupczok's ternary Goldbach mean value theorem with primes in progressions and short intervals, repaired

entries.abstract: We prove an exact four-term probability law for zero-sum maximal-independent-set witnesses. For every connected simple graph G on eight vertices and every admissible eight-point cap U in F_3^3, sample uniformly from all 40,320 bijections of the vertices onto U. Let N0 count zero-sum maximal independent four-sets, m count the size-four maximal independent sets, n0 and n2 count their unordered pairs intersecting in zero and two vertices, and h count compatible unordered triples. Put M1 = 2m/35, M2 = 2n0/35 + n2/315, and M3 = h/315. Then P(N0=0) = 1-M1+M2-M3, P(N0=1) = M1-2M2+3M3, P(N0=2) = M2-3M3, and P(N0=3) = M3 = h/315 <= 1/105; equality holds if and only if G is isomorphic to the spider S(2,2,2,1). In particular N0 <= 3. The theorem does not assume an external cap normal-form classification.
entries.title: Zero-Sum Quartet Incidence and Sharp Maximal-Independent-Set Witnesses on Eight Vertices

entries.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Natural Cohomology of General Steiner Bundles. Over every characteristic-zero field, for all n >= 1, t >= 1, and r >= n, a nonempty principal open of t by (t+r) matrices of linear forms on projective n-space has maximal rank in every homogeneous degree. The transposes give exact Steiner presentations of actual rank-r locally free sheaves, whose integer twists each have at most one nonzero sheaf cohomology group. The coefficient open is nonempty over the original field.
entries.title: Natural cohomology of general Steiner bundles

entries.abstract: Finite planar simple graphs of extended girth at least five are 3-choosable over arbitrary colour types. Includes a complete six-vertex boundary-extension induction, actual induced-face geometry and residual list-colouring infrastructure. Additional results expose the short-path theorem, derive an infinite finite-list compactness consequence, extend arbitrary five/six-cycles, and extend outer seven-cycles. The full original Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 are also proved, including arbitrary allowed fixed-edge colours and all exterior components.
entries.title: Thomassen: planar graphs of girth at least five are 3-choosable

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Lovász, Thomassen, Wu and Zhang: every finite 6-edge-connected simple graph has a nowhere-zero integer 3-flow (the weak 3-flow conjecture). The proof formalizes Theorem 3.1 of the paper (β-orientations of multigraphs modulo 3) and Tutte's lifting theorem. Only simple graphs are stated; the paper's multigraph version and its results on modulo k-orientations for k > 3 are not stated. Mathlib does not contain this theorem.
entries.title: Nowhere-zero 3-flows in 6-edge-connected graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two classical threshold results for the binomial random graph G(n, p), modelled as a finite product probability space with one independent Bernoulli(p) coin per pair of vertices: Pósa's theorem (1976) that G(n, p) with p ≥ C log n / n is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 1, also stated with the explicit constant C = 80 (posa_eighty), and both sides of the Erdős–Rényi connectivity threshold (1959): G(n, (log n ± ω(n))/n) with ω(n) → ∞, the edge probability clipped to [0, 1], is connected with probability tending to 1, resp. 0. Hamiltonicity and connectivity are Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian and SimpleGraph.Connected. Mathlib defines the binomial random graph as a measure on graphs (SimpleGraph.binomialRandom); this project uses its own finite product model instead, and these threshold theorems are not in Mathlib.
entries.title: Hamiltonicity and connectivity thresholds of the random graph G(n, p)

entries.abstract: A subset A of X^J with the property of Baire, invariant under every permutation moving only finitely many indices, is meagre or has meagre complement when J is infinite and the actual product space X^J is Baire. A corollary covers countable products of any Polish space. Finite-support displacement, cylinder mixing and the category contradiction are proved, not assumed.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Category Hewitt–Savage zero-one law for infinite Baire products

entries.abstract: Formalization of a family of pairs of bounded, simply connected, strictly convex planar domains with real-analytic boundaries. At each parameter, the two domains have identical Steklov spectra, including multiplicities. Distinct labels or parameters give noncongruent domains. Each domain has perimeter 2π and no orientation-reversing Euclidean symmetry, and normalized conformal maps converge in C∞ to the identity. The proof uses an explicit degree-seven construction.
entries.title: Strictly Convex Steklov-Isospectral Plane Domains

entries.abstract: For finite primitive-step sets in the scoped geometric computational-path model, actual signed trace periods define a cochain complex. Closedness is equivalent to invariance under the entire scoped rewrite relation. Orthogonal projection constructs the unique harmonic representative of every degree-one presentation cohomology class, preserves all loop periods, and induces an actual linear equivalence. Vanishing of all loop periods is equivalent to being a coboundary, without connectivity assumptions; periods separate cohomology and harmonic representatives. A nonzero parallel-edge model and a named-rewrite control expose the distinction from ambient geometric homotopy. Discrete presentation cohomology only, not analytic or Kahler Hodge theory.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Harmonic representatives and period separation for computational-path presentations

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Pippenger and Spencer (1989): for r ≥ 2 and ε > 0 there are μ > 0 and D₀ such that every r-uniform hypergraph whose degrees lie in [(1 − μ)D, D] and whose codegrees are at most μD, with D ≥ D₀, has chromatic index at most (1 + ε)D. A second theorem gives an explicit polynomial error: if the maximum degree is at most D, the codegrees are at most D^{1−δ} and there are at most exp(D^γ) edges, then the chromatic index is at most D + D^{1−γ} for some γ = γ(r, δ) > 0. The proofs build on the author's registered formalization of Ehard–Glock–Joos (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000004): batches of the trimmed Rödl nibble with the Lovász Local Lemma for the first theorem, and the pseudorandom matching theorem (Ehard–Glock–Joos, Theorem 1.2) applied to an auxiliary colour hypergraph for the second. Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: The Pippenger–Spencer theorem on the chromatic index of hypergraphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three classical results on graphs with large chromatic number. (1) Erdős' 1959 theorem: for every g and k there is a finite graph with girth greater than g and chromatic number greater than k, in the structural form given by the probabilistic argument (for every ε > 0 and all large n, a graph on n vertices with girth greater than g whose independent sets have fewer than εn vertices). (2) Mycielski's 1955 construction M(G): it preserves and reflects triangle-freeness, M(G) is (k+1)-colourable exactly when G is k-colourable, χ(M(G)) = χ(G) + 1 for every finite G, and iterating from K₂ gives triangle-free graphs with 3·2ⁿ − 1 vertices and chromatic number n + 2. (3) Larsen, Propp and Ullman (1995): for the fractional chromatic number χ_f (least total weight of a fractional colouring by independent sets), χ_f(M(G)) = χ_f(G) + 1/χ_f(G) for every finite graph G with at least one vertex. Version 2 adds (2) and (3); the statements of version 1 are unchanged. Mathlib has girth and chromatic number but none of these theorems, and no fractional chromatic number.
entries.title: Graphs of large girth and large chromatic number: Erdős, Mycielski, and the fractional chromatic number of Mycielski graphs

entries.abstract: Pratt (STOC 2024, arXiv:2311.02774, Corollary 1.12) showed that if the Set Cover Conjecture holds, then for every k the asymptotic rank of the balanced tripartitioning tensor T_k is at least tau_k = 8^k * C(3k,k) * C(2k,k) / 27^k. A natural way to bound this rank, and Pratt's own route to rank at most 8^k/2, is a group construction: maps f1, f2, f3 from k-subsets of a 3k-set to a group G with f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = 1 exactly when A, B, C are pairwise disjoint (a partition analogue of the Cohn-Umans triple product property). We formalise that no such construction, in any finite group, abelian or not, can refute the conjecture: |G| > tau_k for every k >= 2. The same holds for Strassen combinatorial degenerations of group tensors (border-rank constructions), via |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2)) > tau_k. The proof formalises a rigidity theorem: the triple products always factor through pairwise commuting elements, f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = prod_i g_i^(m_i - 1) with m the multiplicity vector, so non-abelian groups give no advantage, unlike in the Cohn-Umans approach to matrix multiplication. It also formalises a lift lemma giving |G| >= 2^(3k-1), which shows Pratt's 8^k/2 is exactly optimal among group restrictions. Pratt's Corollary 1.12 and the passage from a group embedding to a rank bound are cited, not formalised. The bounds concern the group size needed by such constructions, not the rank of T_k itself. Joint constructions for tensor powers are covered: a degeneration of a group tensor onto T_k^(tensor m) needs |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2))^m > tau_k^m, so the induced asymptotic-rank bound |G|^(1/m) stays above tau_k.
entries.title: Group constructions cannot refute the Set Cover Conjecture, including tensor powers

entries.abstract: CONDITIONAL. A Lean 4 proof that, under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, every even integer N at least exp(exp 13.375) is the sum of a prime and a square-free number greater than 1 with at most two prime factors, CONDITIONAL ON four cited results taken as explicit hypotheses of the theorem, never as axioms: Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J, the Lean Lab's transcriptions of Theorems 5, 6 and 7 of M. Bordignon and V. Starichkova, An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Ramanujan J. 64, 2024, 1213 to 1242; and LinearSieveT4 1/8349 112 114, the transcription of their Theorem 4, the explicit linear sieve of Bordignon, Johnston and Starichkova with the Table 1 row epsilon inverse 6100, C1 = 112, C2 = 114. These transcriptions use the Lean normalisation U_N = 2 e^{-gamma} times the product over p > 2 of 1 - 1/(p-1)^2 times the product over p > 2 dividing N of (p-1)/(p-2), while the journal prints U_N without the factor 2; see the fidelity section. GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is the premise inside the conclusion ChenThreshold13375. The journal's own Corollary 1 has the threshold exp(exp 14); the threshold exp(exp 13.375) comes from re-choosing the Section 5.4 parameters inside the authors' method, alpha = 0.00256, A = 10, u = 1500, epsilon = 1/8349, epsilon1 = 10^-20. The numeric inputs are PROVED here: epsilon(1500) is below 1/8349 by a kernel certificate, decide +kernel in eleven window modules, and the Section 5.4 bracket combination is at least the main-term constant minus 10^-5, a one-sided lower bound. Chen's weighted inequality, the journal's Lemma 9, is PROVED unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote all the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: CONDITIONAL on GRH and four cited theorems: an explicit Chen threshold exp(exp 13.375), after Bordignon and Starichkova

entries.abstract: Formalization of Chang's version of Freiman's theorem, with a 2-proper progression P: a finite set X of integers with |X + X| <= kappa |X| is contained in a 2-proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most the Freiman dimension of X, hence at most 2 kappa - 1, with at most exp(10^32 kappa^7) |X| points. If kappa (2 kappa - 1) <= epsilon |X|, the dimension is at most floor(kappa - 1 + epsilon), as in Green and Tao. There is also a statement for subsets of ZMod q with q prime, where the progression has at most exp(10^30 kappa^7) |X| points. The bound on the size is weaker than that of Chang. The first step of the proof, the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, is stated too: if moreover |X| >= 7 * 10^7 kappa^2, then 2X - 2X contains a proper progression of dimension at most 3 * 10^5 kappa^2 with at least exp(-2 * 10^7 kappa^2) |X| points.
entries.title: Chang's version of Freiman's theorem and the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, against Mathlib, that one deterministic Turing machine computes the smallest prime factor Nat.minFac N of every natural number N in time N^{o(1)}: for every k >= 1 there is a constant C_k such that the same machine halts with the correct output within C_k * 2^(n/k) steps on every n-bit input. The machine model is Mathlib's Turing machine model TM2 (Turing.FinTM2 with Turing.TM2ComputableInTime), with numbers in binary (Computability.encodeNat) and every stack alphabet finite. The best previously published deterministic bounds known to the authors have exponent 1/5 (Harvey 2021; Harvey and Hittmeir 2022). The proof reduces finding the smallest prime factor to counting divisors with prescribed leading bits, expresses that count as the value of a network of local checks carrying out Schoenhage-Strassen multiplication, and evaluates it with a re-proved form of the counting engine of the 2026 3-SAT preprint by Claude (Anthropic). The Challenge also states, as a proposition only and without proof, a conjecture that factoring can be done in time exp(O(log N / sqrt(log log N))). The ideas and the Lean code were generated by AI; the authors audited the statement, not the proof.
entries.title: Deterministic factoring in time N^{o(1)}

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of "The Critical 2D KPZ Process" by Berger, Caravenna, Clark, Dunlap, Gu, Liu, Nakajima, Sun, Tsai, Xie and Zygouras (arXiv:2610.31614, version 1), together with selected inputs and adaptations in the form these proofs need. For directed polymers on Z^2 in a Gaussian environment at critical disorder, it proves the existence of a critical 2D stochastic heat flow, defined as the joint limit in law of the rescaled partition functions (Theorem A). The centred log-partition function converges in law, in the local negative Sobolev spaces H^{-a}_loc and jointly in finitely many times and initial data, to the critical 2D KPZ process (Theorem 1.2). The process satisfies the comparison principle in the initial data. For flat initial data, its averages at scale epsilon, divided by sqrt(log log(1/epsilon)), converge in law to a centred Gaussian (Theorem 1.4(i)); it has a radial covariance kernel equivalent to log log(1/|z|) at the diagonal (Theorem 1.4(ii)), is not a signed measure (Proposition 1.5), is not Gaussian (Theorem 1.6), is invariant under translations and rotations and covariant under scaling (Proposition 1.8), and its pairing with each nonnegative test function has a law of Ehrhard type (Proposition 3.8). It also proves strict skewness, twice differentiable response to initial data, Brownian motion across scales and the finite-dimensional GFF tangent (Theorems A–D of Scott Armstrong’s note). The parameter theta is fixed. Built on Mathlib. All proofs use only Lean's standard axioms.
entries.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the paper "Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six" by Manvir Jaswal. Theorem 1.1 says that infinitely many elliptic curves over Q have torsion subgroup Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six, with infinitely many distinct j-invariants. The curves are fibers of a one-parameter family of Dujella and Peral, y² = x(x + a²)(x + b²), which has rank three over Q(m) and gains three further independent points over the function field of a curve C of genus one; congruences carry the independence of the six points, and the torsion, from one rational point of C to infinitely many. Theorem 1.2 shows that the smooth projective model of C is isomorphic over Q to an elliptic curve of conductor 9240 and rank one, that the family has rank exactly six over Q(C), and that at all but finitely many rational points of C its fibers have torsion exactly Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six. Theorem 8.1 gives a second such family, over a curve of genus one whose Jacobian has rank two. All 19 numbered results of the paper are proved. The theorems take published theorems of other authors as hypotheses, each stated in general form, about no curve or surface of the paper; Theorem 1.1 takes four: Mazur's torsion theorem, the integrality of torsion points at odd primes, that reduction at a prime of good reduction is a homomorphism, and that the points of an elliptic curve over Q_p form a compact topological group. Comparator checks Theorem 1.1; the other results are proved in the same library.
entries.title: Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six

entries.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 3 of On t-designs (1975): a k-uniform family of subsets of an n-element ground set whose distinct-pair intersection sizes lie in L ⊆ {0,...,k−1} has at most binomial(n,|L|) members. Includes the actual-intersection-spectrum formulation, the uniform one-intersection bound, and equality examples consisting of all s-subsets.
entries.title: Ray-Chaudhuri–Wilson: uniform families with restricted intersections

entries.abstract: Every nonempty open subset U of a perfect Polish space X contains a closed topological embedding e of Cantor space Nat -> Bool such that every ordered pair of distinct image points lies in each member of a countable family of dense-open subsets R_n of X × X. Coordinated finite refinements enforce all ordered pairs, have closure nesting and vanishing diameter; ambient completeness yields the Cantor limit map. Single-Cantor binary-relation scope only; no novelty claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Mycielski Cantor independent set for dense-open binary relations

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Edmonds' theorems (1965) for finite simple graphs: the convex hull of the incidence vectors of the perfect matchings is {x ≥ 0, x(δ(v)) = 1 for every vertex v, x(δ(S)) ≥ 1 for every odd set S}, and the convex hull of the incidence vectors of all matchings is {x ≥ 0, x(δ(v)) ≤ 1, x(E[S]) ≤ (|S| − 1)/2 for every odd S}. Vectors are indexed by the edges of the graph, the convex hull is Mathlib's convexHull, and matchings are Mathlib's Subgraph.IsMatching and Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching. The perfect matching theorem is proved for multigraphs by induction with shrinking of tight odd cuts; the matching polytope follows by the doubling construction. Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: Edmonds' perfect matching polytope and matching polytope

entries.abstract: For every finite simple graph and k ≥ 0, the signed evaluation (−1)^n χ_G(−k) counts acyclic orientations paired with weakly compatible Fin k colorings (Stanley 1973, Theorem 1.2); at k = 1 it counts acyclic orientations (Corollary 1.3). Includes positive-evaluation correctness, induced-subgraph convolution, and the finite equivalence between well-foundedness and no directed cycles.
entries.title: Stanley's acyclic orientations and chromatic reciprocity

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of nonuniqueness for the unforced incompressible Euler equations on the two-dimensional square torus. For each finite real exponent p at least one and each positive time interval, the selected theorem constructs a common mean-zero, divergence-free initial datum in L2 and W1p, and two distinct weak solutions continuous in time with values in L2. Their distributional vorticities have strongly measurable Lp-valued representatives that are essentially bounded in time. This is the two-dimensional finite-Lp question in the first part of Buckmaster and Vicol's Problem 6. The full proof and reproducibility checks have passed.
entries.title: Finite-Lp vorticity nonuniqueness for two-dimensional Euler

entries.abstract: Every homeomorphism of a closed nowhere-dense subset A of the usual Cantor space Nat -> Bool extends pointwise to an ambient homeomorphism H with a dense forward orbit. Empty A is included. The proof constructs an orbit embedding into the two-sided full shift, extends it using Knaster–Reichbach, proves forward shift orbit density by finite-coordinate patching and Baire, and conjugates back. Classical invariant-subset case only; no novelty claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Cantor dynamical extension with a dense forward orbit

entries.abstract: Every homeomorphism between closed nowhere-dense subsets of Cantor space extends to a homeomorphism of the entire Cantor space, with exact pointwise agreement. Cantor space is the usual product topology on Nat -> Bool. Empty prescribed subsets are included. The proof constructs matched finite clopen refinements by alternating binary coordinate splits, then obtains mutually inverse continuous limit maps. Classical result; no novelty or priority claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Knaster–Reichbach homeomorphism extension on Cantor space

entries.abstract: Cardinality min-max theorem for two finite Mathlib matroids with the same ground, attained primal-dual certificates, exact-size feasibility and the equal-rank common-base criterion.
entries.title: Edmonds cardinality matroid intersection

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Nash-Williams' weak orientation theorem (1960): every 2k-edge-connected finite graph has a k-arc-connected orientation, i.e. one in which every nonempty proper vertex set is left by at least k arcs. It is proved for finite loopless multigraphs given by an edge family, and stated for simple graphs with Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsEdgeConnected and orientations as Mathlib Digraphs. The proof is by induction on the number of edges, with Mader's lemma (a minimally 2k-edge-connected multigraph has a vertex of degree 2k) and Lovász's splitting lemma, both proved in the project. Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: Nash-Williams' weak orientation theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kirkman's 1847 theorem: for v ≥ 1, a Steiner triple system on v points (a family of 3-subsets covering every pair of distinct points exactly once) exists if and only if v ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 6). Sufficiency is proved by Bose's and Skolem's constructions from Steiner quasigroups. Mathlib does not contain Steiner triple systems.
entries.title: Kirkman's theorem on Steiner triple systems

entries.abstract: CONDITIONAL. A Lean 4 proof that, under the Riemann Hypothesis, for every real x at least 3 there is a Goldbach number n, a sum of two odd primes, with x < n < x + 4.45 (log x)^2. This improves the constant 123 of A. Chirre and M. V. Hagen, On Goldbach numbers in short intervals, arXiv 2512.23534, by their method. RH is the paper's own hypothesis. The theorem is CONDITIONAL ON seven cited inputs taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, all stated for gZ, the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function counted with multiplicity: ExplicitA, the truncated explicit formula of Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, display 12.1, under RH; HadamardK, the bound sum over gamma' of 4/(4 + (gamma - gamma')^2) at most log |gamma|, a consequence of the Hadamard product, under RH; Ordinates14, every ordinate at least 14 in absolute value; BPTN, the zero count of Brent, Platt and Trudgian, J. Number Theory 238, 2022, Lemma 1, for T at least 10^13; HSWN70 and HSWHead14, the zero count of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, arXiv 2107.06506, Corollary 1.2, for T at least 70 and T at least 14; and EvenGoldbachUpTo 4*10^18, the verification of the even Goldbach conjecture to 4*10^18 by Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, Math. Comp. 83, 2014. These are the Lean Lab's transcriptions, not Mathlib results. Everything else in the argument is proved: Theorem 2 of Chirre and Hagen with the diagonal constant lowered to 1.0068, the passage from psi to theta, and their Section 5. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote the Lean code, with the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; the statements were checked against the papers by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: CONDITIONAL on RH and cited zero counts: Goldbach numbers in intervals of length 4.45 log^2 x

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hilton–Milner theorem: for k ≥ 2 and n > 2k, a nontrivial intersecting family of k-subsets of an n-set (no element lies in all members) has at most C(n−1, k−1) − C(n−k−1, k−1) + 1 members, and this bound is attained. Intersecting is Mathlib's Set.Intersecting. Mathlib contains the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem but not this result.
entries.title: The Hilton–Milner theorem

entries.abstract: There exist a countable group G and a nontrivial finite alphabet A such that the ordinary left Bernoulli shifts on A and A times A, equipped with their uniform product probability measures, are equivariantly measure-preservingly isomorphic on invariant conull measurable sets. The inverse is measurable. The finite alphabets have different cardinalities and therefore different uniform base Shannon entropies. The algebraic existence input is supplied by the pinned OpenAI proofs. This formalization does not certify all-base collapse, finitary continuity, the integer coding inputs, or the manuscript's later corollaries.
entries.title: Finite uniform Bernoulli shifts with unequal base entropy

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the main results of Abedin, Feldman and Stinson on Perron's extremal solutions of the one-phase Bernoulli free boundary problem Δu = 0 in {u > 0} ∩ U, |∇u| = Q on ∂{u > 0} ∩ U. Let U ⊂ ℝᵈ, d ≥ 2, be open, bounded and connected with C² boundary, and let Q be Lipschitz on the closure of U with 0 < Q_min ≤ Q ≤ Q_max. Theorem 1.1: the smallest supersolution above a smooth strict subsolution g with g > 0 on ∂U is (i) a viscosity solution in U, (ii) an inner variational solution in U for some χ (the first domain variation of the Alt–Caffarelli energy ∫ |∇u|² + Q² χ vanishes), and (iii) a downward minimizer of that energy on a ball around each free boundary point; the largest subsolution below a smooth strict supersolution g has the same three properties, with upward minimality in (iii). Corollary 1.2, in ℝ²: (i) the free boundary of the smallest supersolution is the disjoint union of a relatively open set, near each point of which u is a classical solution (a C^{1,γ} free boundary, u harmonic in {u > 0}, ∇u continuous up to the free boundary with |∇u| = Q there), and a set at each point x₀ of which every blow-up limit of u is the two-plane function Q(x₀)|y · e| for some unit vector e; (ii) the largest subsolution is a classical solution near every free boundary point. Every notion, including viscosity solutions, smooth strict sub- and supersolutions, Perron's classes, inner variational solutions, Sobolev functions, the one-sided minimizers, blow-up limits and classical solutions, is written out from Mathlib definitions. A fifth statement is the necklace example, a rigorous version, with different parameters, of the numerical example in Figure 1 of the paper: in ℝ² with Q ≡ 1 there are a domain and data, with the same boundary values for both problems, whose smallest supersolution and largest subsolution are both nontrivial and differ on a set of positive measure, the smallest supersolution has a two-plane point, and a minimizer of the Alt–Caffarelli energy with the same boundary data exists and differs from both extremal solutions on sets of positive measure. It also shows that the hypotheses of the other statements can be met and that their conclusions are not degenerate.
entries.title: Perron's extremal solutions of the Bernoulli one-phase problem: viscosity, inner variational and one-sided minimizing solutions, and free boundary structure in the plane

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture, "weak normalization implies strong normalization", for the pure type systems PTS_βη of Geuvers (Logics and Type Systems, 1993), whose conversion rule uses βη-conversion. For every PTS specification, with no functionality assumption, it proves two theorems about the legal terms of PTS_βη. If every legal term is weakly βη-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. If every legal term is weakly β-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. The proof adapts OpenAI's 2026 proof of the β case for PTS_β, whose Lean files are included. An η-step can delete a λ-annotation, so the proof works from a weaker hypothesis, that every legal term has a β-reduct with no β-redex outside its λ-domains. Conversion is handled through domain erasure, candidates are indexed by βη-normal forms of erased types, and observation values are made η-canonical.
entries.title: Weak and strong βη-normalization in pure type systems with βη-conversion

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization (found by Codex GPT 5.6 Sol) of the main theorem of the author's recent arxiv preprint	arXiv:2608.26321.  This is the Birthday Paradox for non-backtracking walks on regular graphs of degree at least 3: such a walk of length k has high probability of self-intersecting when k is significantly greater than sqrt(n), where n is the number of vertices of the graph. This resolves a conjecture of Noga Alon and Yuval Peres for the fixed degree case.
entries.title: birthday-paradox-non-backtracking-regular-graphs

entries.abstract: For every pair a ≥ b ≥ 1 there is a straight-line derivation of gcd(a, b) that uses only the remainder operation on available values and makes at most (3 + o(1)) log₂ a / log₂ log₂ a remainder calls, uniformly in b ≤ a; Euclid's algorithm needs about 1.44 log₂ a calls in the worst case. The proof stores a prefix of the Euclidean remainder sequence, shows that modulo every sufficiently large modulus at most three of its values share a residue class, and uses close residues to shrink the modulus by three remainder calls at a time. Consequently the intrinsic calls(rem)-complexities of the gcd and of coprimeness, in the sense of Moschovakis's Abstract Recursion and Intrinsic Complexity, are O(log a / log log a). This refutes Conjecture 3.4 of Moschovakis's 2012 notes "Absolute lower bounds for uniform processes" and the version (4F-5) of the Main Conjecture in the book, both for the structure (ℕ, rem, eq0) and for Nε = (ℕ, rem, eq0, eq1). The same bound answers negatively the closure-depth question of van den Dries and Moschovakis (2009): there are no positive integers aₙ → ∞, bₙ and C > 0 whose closure depth g(aₙ, bₙ) exceeds C log₂ aₙ for all n. For algorithms, the library gives fixed nondeterministic register programs over (ℕ, rem, eq0) with arbitrarily small logarithmic coefficients: for each ε > 0, one program with 3·2^p + 6 registers (any p > 3/ε) and no recursion stack has, on every input a ≥ b ≥ 1, a convergent computation returning gcd(a, b) with at most ε log₂ a + B remainder calls, and the same program written one function per line is a tail-recursive program with bounded stacks. These programs depend on ε, so the Main Conjecture for algorithms (deterministic or nondeterministic recursive programs) is not settled and remains open. Lower bounds are also formalized: every gcd certificate needs at least as many remainder facts as the shortest derivation, and the coprimeness complexity is at least (1 − ε) log₂ log₂ N on all but o(N²) coprime pairs below N.
entries.title: The Euclidean algorithm is not optimal among uniform processes

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Version 2 adds Theorem A, eq 3.113: for every r at least 3 and every Theta with 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4, on the paper's own Hypothesis R at level Theta, that no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above Theta, nu_r of n equals the singular series S_r of n of 3.114 times n^{r-1} over the factorial of r minus 1, plus O of n^{r-1+Theta-3/4} times a power of log n, for all n from some n0. The paper allows every Theta below 3/4; the Lean statement covers only 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4. The entry also proves derived results on Theorem A that are not statements of the paper: its hypotheses other than the zero-free one hold together, GRH gives the zero-free hypothesis for every Theta at least 1/2, Theorem A at Theta equal to 47/64 on GRH, and S_r of n is positive with a summable series in like parity. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were written from the paper's page images by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R, and Theorem A on Hypothesis R for 47/64 at most Theta below 3/4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow, "The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete" (J. ACM 2021), together with Stade's point-boundary variant (SoCG 2025), for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model. Lean proves that deciding whether a simple polygon with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions in each of the three variants known to be ∃ℝ-complete: point guards guarding the whole polygon (Theorem 1, also for integer corners), guards on the boundary guarding the whole polygon (the boundary-point variant of the paper's §7.2), and point guards guarding only the boundary (Stade's theorem); that ETR-INV is ∃ℝ-complete; that the guard sets of the paper's Section 5 polygon correspond exactly to the solutions of an ETR-INV instance (Theorem 54, with the range condition made explicit) and encode the solutions of any ETR formula (Theorem 55); that every real algebraic number is the x-coordinate of a guard in every optimal guard set of some polygon with rational corners (Theorem 2); and that some x-monotone polygon with integer corners can be guarded by three guards but needs four rational guards (Theorem 4). The development provides reusable material on the existential theory of the reals: formulas and their codes, the class ∃ℝ, ETR-INV and ETR-INV-REV with polynomial-time reductions from ETR, and an elementary proof of the doubly exponential solution bound that the paper cites from Schaefer and Štefankovič. It partially answers the open problem of the paper's §7.2 on the number of variables: all three art gallery problems reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards (the paper uses (n+g)^6 variables for n corners). Point-point and point-boundary hardness is proved through Stade's construction; the paper's own Section 5 construction is formalized for Theorems 54 and 55, with gadget visibility facts checked as kernel-evaluated certificates, and a modification of it (guard segments on shallow bays in the boundary, re-laid-out addition gadgets) gives boundary-point hardness. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete: point-point, boundary-point and point-boundary variants, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Symmetry-weighted enumeration of finite facet-pairing diagrams and polytope trees: cut-join recurrences, factorial formulas, formal exponential generating functions, local analytic counting series with specified radical branches, binomial identities and asymptotic equivalents. The development also proves unique extension of intrinsic facet isometries for finite spanning flag-regular Euclidean cells, derives their geometric presentation masses, and proves an exponential lower bound for ordinary simplicial triangulation classes from any fixed finite pure triangulation of dimension at least two.
entries.title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond — Lean 4 formalization

entries.abstract: In graph pebbling, a move removes two pebbles from a vertex and adds one to a neighbour; a configuration is stackable if moves can bring all pebbles onto one vertex and clearable if moves can leave exactly one pebble. The stacking (clearing) number of a connected (connected non-bipartite) graph is the least t >= 2 such that every configuration of t pebbles is stackable (clearable). The Almost Stacked Hypothesis, in its critical form, says that this number equals the least t0 >= 2 such that every almost stacked configuration (one vertex arbitrary, every other vertex at most one pebble) of every size at least t0 is stackable (clearable). We formalise a counterexample to both clauses: on the nine-vertex graph G9 (graph6 HCQTaXi) the stacking and clearing numbers are 15, the only non-stackable and non-clearable configurations of size 14 are (0,0,1,0,0,5,0,8,0) and its automorphic image, neither almost stacked, while every almost stacked configuration of size at least 14 is stackable and clearable. Hence neither clause holds for all finite connected (respectively connected non-bipartite) graphs. The finite facts are proved by kernel evaluation (decide +kernel) of a verified exact losing-layer checker on certificate data; general lemmas (clearable implies stackable; monotonicity above the order) are proved by hand.
entries.title: The critical Almost Stacked Hypothesis fails on a nine-vertex graph

entries.abstract: A polyhex is an edge-to-edge connected system of cells of the regular hexagonal tiling. Kurz (Convex hulls of polyominoes, Beiträge Algebra Geom. 49 (2008), Conjecture 2) conjectured that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells of unit area has area at most ⌊n² + 14n/3 + 1⌋ / 6. This formalization proves the conjecture, and the sharper bound ⌈n² + 14n/3⌉ / 6, which differs from Kurz's bound by 1/6 when 3 divides n and agrees with it otherwise. The statements are made in the Euclidean plane for the regular hexagonal tiling, with area measured in units of one cell. The proof writes the hull as the hull of the cell centres plus one hexagon, bounds its area through the area of the centre hull and three of its widths, and controls both with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The accompanying paper (arXiv:2609.30310) also shows that the sharp bound is attained for every n by a path made of three straight runs, so that it is the exact maximum. That construction is not formalized.
entries.title: Kurz's conjecture on the maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex

entries.abstract: For a vector v with nonnegative entries and a real number p, write v^p for the vector of p-th powers of its entries. Johnston, Plosker, Torrance and Varona (arXiv:2507.10327, Conjecture 5.1) conjectured that ‖v^p‖ ‖w^p‖ - ⟨v^p, w^p⟩ ≤ ‖v‖^p ‖w‖^p - ⟨v, w⟩^p for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors v, w in ℝⁿ with positive entries, with the Euclidean norm and inner product. They proved it for integer p and showed that it fails for 1 < p < 2. This formalization proves the conjecture for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors with nonnegative entries. It also determines every case of equality: for p > 2 equality holds exactly when v and w are linearly dependent or each has at most one nonzero entry, and for p = 2 there is one further family supported on two coordinates. Finally, for positive coordinate weights ω used in every norm and inner product, the weighted inequality holds for all nonnegative vectors exactly when ω_i ω_j ≥ 1 for all i ≠ j, a condition that does not depend on p. The proof shows that a 2 × 2 entrywise-power defect matrix is positive semidefinite, using a double integral formula and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for integrals. The conjecture and its equality cases were also proved, independently and concurrently, by Johnston and Sababheh (arXiv:2610.12063).
entries.title: A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers: proof, equality cases and weighted forms

entries.abstract: Erdős Problem 699 (Erdős and Szekeres 1978) asks whether for every 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n/2 there is a prime p ≥ i dividing gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)). The problem is open. Using the statement from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures with the single extra hypothesis j² < n, this project proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that the answer is yes whenever j² < n; equivalently, every counterexample (n, i, j) has n ≤ j². The proof combines the Erdős–Szekeres inequality gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)) ≥ C(n, i)/C(j, i) ≥ (n/j)^i, which follows from the identity C(n, j) C(j, i) = C(n, i) C(n − i, j − i), with an upper bound for a gcd whose prime factors are all below i: each prime power in C(n, i) is at most n (Kummer), and there are at most i/2 primes below i, so such a gcd is at most n^(i/2). The bound reduces the problem to j ≥ √n. With a computer search of every n < 10^12 (not part of this formalization) it rules out counterexamples with j ≤ 10^6. The argument is short and may well be folklore; formal-conjectures records the problem but no partial result of this kind.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 699: every counterexample has n ≤ j²

entries.abstract: For actual commuting integer-indexed double complexes over a field, componentwise image/kernel identities imply biclosed representatives of vertical cohomology classes and vanishing of every higher differential of the column-filtered signed total complex. The genuine first quotient page identifies with vertical cohomology; canonical recurrence agrees on actual representatives and covers all next-page classes. Finite rectangular support gives actual quotient stabilization and a canonical identification with the associated graded of total cohomology with its finite, exhaustive, separated induced filtration. Classical conditional algebraic mathematics; no analytic compact-Kähler theorem or novelty claim.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Algebraic E1 degeneration from explicit d′d″ identities

entries.abstract: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. The mechanism is a matching lemma: for sign functions sigma, tau and a bijection pi, the correlation sum sigma(x) tau(pi x) is congruent modulo 4 to the sum of the two marginals minus the number of terms, so it does not depend on pi. Along the way it proves the parity dictionary (-1)^floor(n^2/p) = s(n) s(n^2) with s(x) = (-1)^<x>, the coset form f = sum over the fourth powers H of s(u) s(u^2) and e = the same sum over 2H, the lag identity sum over 2H of s(u) s(2u) = kappa exactly, the exact coset parities sum_H s = k + 2t and sum_{2H} s = t - 2k where B_{1,chi} = k + i t, and the Coordinate Congruence kappa = (p-1)/4 + k + t (mod 4). It also proves the odd-subgroup congruence: for an odd modulus N >= 3, a subgroup H of (Z/N)^x of odd order h, a coset X = xH and an even exponent e >= 2, the band-parity sum of X and -X over (0, N/2) equals sum over X of s(u) s(u^e) and is congruent to h - 2 alpha(X) - 2 alpha(X^e) modulo 4, where alpha counts elements with odd least residue.
entries.title: BandParity: the band-parity sum of a quartic character, two laws modulo 4

entries.abstract: For integers 0 < b < a, let P(a,b) count the positive terms obtained by repeatedly replacing x by a mod x, starting at b. This development proves the uniform bound P(a,b) ≤ C_ε a^((41301 - 3 sqrt(82849))/137480 + ε) for every ε > 0, including the external coefficient-uniform affine-curve theorem and the effective Hilbert specialisation sieve, and its rational instance 4317/14677. It also proves the exterior-lattice exponents 471/1559 - 6 sqrt(105)/7795 and 153/520, the joint-invariant exponents (1310-sqrt(655))/4365, 2201/7480 and 128/435 and the earlier exponents 45/152, 8/27, 11/37, 23/77, and 3/10. It also proves a bound O(a^(1/4) sqrt R), where R minus one counts rises in the quotient increments, and positivity and integrality of the orbit's Hankel invariants. A separate conditional theorem gives O(a^(3/10) sqrt(log log(3a))) assuming two explicitly stated analytic estimates whose proofs are not formalised. The polar bound uses the proved orbit identity, actual common-base bound of four, degree-twelve residue labels, uniform arithmetic specialisation count, and full-pattern completion count with arbitrary common divisors. These establish the six-term local estimate without additional hypotheses. The conjectured O((log a)^2) bound remains open.
entries.title: Bounds for the iteration x ↦ a mod x

entries.abstract: Conditional Lean formalisation of “Independent sets in hypergraphs with no loose triangle” by Ayush Basu, Abhishek Dhawan and Abhishek Methuku. Assuming the explicitly stated normalized Li–Postle vertex-coloring bound for triangle-free hypergraphs with edges of sizes 3 and 4, for every fixed integer r >= 3 there are constants c > 0 and N such that every n-vertex hypergraph with n >= N, edge sizes between 3 and r, and no loose triangle has an independent set of size at least c n^(2/3) (log log n)^(1/3). The implication is proved in Lean; the Li–Postle premise and the manuscript's Ramsey corollary are not proved in this development.
entries.title: Independent sets in hypergraphs with no loose triangle

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Random walk on sphere packings and Delaunay triangulations in arbitrary dimension" by Bou-Rabee and Gwynne: on orthogonal tilings with small mesh and one of three regularity hypotheses, the stopped conductance-weighted random walk converges to stopped Brownian motion modulo time parametrization (Theorem A) and the discrete Dirichlet problem converges (Theorem B, both alternatives); Poisson-Voronoi tessellations satisfy the hypotheses (Proposition 1.1); and simple random walk on a bounded-degree sphere packing need not converge (Theorem 6.1); for any nearest-neighbour walks under Assumption D the stopped walk converges to stopped Brownian motion (Theorem 4.1). Every labelled result is registered and proved, as printed or as in the corrected paper (paper/rw-spheres-corrected.tex), where the printed statement is false, not well defined, or changed with the published version open (README.md); Lemma 5.1(b) is registered with dimension-dependent constants, which is weaker than the printed statement in dimensions 4 to 12, where the printed radius also holds but is not needed. Theorem A and Theorem B(a) are Leonardo Bonanno's (leobon12) formalization, imported with attribution.
entries.title: Random walk on sphere packings and Delaunay triangulations in arbitrary dimension

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the local well-posedness and convergence of the renormalised dynamical Phi^4_3 model on the three-dimensional torus, after Hairer's Theorem 1.15. For smooth initial data, explicit renormalisation constants built from the massive heat kernel, and every exponent eta in (-2/3, -1/2), the solutions of the equation driven by mollified space-time white noise converge in probability in the Hölder–Besov space C^eta up to the maximal existence time of the limit, and the limit does not depend on the mollifier. A standalone library proves the general theory used: the reconstruction theorem (Hairer, Theorem 3.10; Hoshino, Theorem 4.1), weighted reconstruction, the multilevel Schauder estimate (Hairer, Theorem 5.12), maximal solutions, and Malliavin calculus for white noise.
entries.title: Regularity structures and dynamical Phi^4_3

entries.abstract: A formalization of a corollary of Theorem 1.2 of arXiv:2609.12688v1.  A C0-semigroup on a separable Hilbert space can admit a stochastic  convolution that has no continuous modification.
entries.title: Discontinuity of stochastic convolutions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Dynamic dimensional reduction in the Abelian sandpile" by Bou-Rabee (Comm. Math. Phys. 390 (2022); arXiv:2009.05968), in a corrected edition of the arXiv source: dimensional reduction and self-similarity of the parallel toppling odometer (Theorem 1.1), the corresponding statements for the sandpile (Corollary 1.1) and the regularity proposition (Proposition 4.1) proved with them by one joint induction over dimension, side length and time, together with every lemma, corollary and proposition of Sections 2 and 3. The main results are stated as published. The four Mathlib-only comparator pairs under DimRedAudit/ check Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.1 and Proposition 4.1.
entries.title: Dynamic dimensional reduction in the Abelian sandpile

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the paper "Once-reinforced random walk on Z^d has range exponent at least d/(d+1)" by Bou-Rabee and Peres: for d >= 2 and reinforcement beta >= 1, the expected range of once-reinforced random walk is at least c beta^(-d/(d+1)) n^(d/(d+1)) (Theorem 1.1), with a stretched-exponential lower tail (Theorem 1.2), the almost-sure bound it implies, and a bound on the occupation measure (Theorem 1.3). Every lemma and proposition behind them is formalized as well, and nothing is assumed. The four main theorems are independently checked using the ORRWAudit/ comparator pairs.
entries.title: ORRW-Lower-Bound

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of every theorem, lemma and proposition of "Unique continuation on planar graphs" (Bou-Rabee, Cooperman and Ganguly): a harmonic function on a periodic plane graph with periodic conductances that is bounded by one on a set of density at least 1 - epsilon is constant (Theorem 1.1), together with the exponential upper bound (Theorem 1.2), the zero case (Theorem 1.3), the topological lemma, the exponential lower bound of the appendix with its polynomial approximation lemma and three-ball proposition, and non-planar periodic conductances on Z^2 with a harmonic function supported on a diagonal (Theorem 5.1).  Three results the paper cites from the literature (Janiszewski's theorem at a point, unicoherence of the sphere and the discrete Moser estimate) are explicit hypotheses of the theorems that use them; the classical Liouville theorem for periodic networks and the discrete Remez inequality are proved. The four main theorems are independently checked using the UCPlanarAudit/ comparator pairs.
entries.title: Unique-Continuation-Planar

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 7.3 of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. At every strictly convex central configuration of four positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least two thirds of its radial part K, and strictly so wherever K is positive. In the notation of the paper this is λ_max(G) < 1/3 for the explicit 2×2 matrix G of its Proposition 3.5, and by its Proposition 7.2 the constant 2/3 is optimal. It sharpens Theorem B of the paper, Q ≥ K/4. The definitions and the reduction to the normal form of Corbera, Cors and Roberts are those of the registered development lean4body-uniqueness. The new parts are a majorant that pays only the largest eigenvalue of S(y), an exact test that is positive definite exactly when λ_max(G) < 1/3, and a computer-assisted proof of that test: a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, reduced by a symmetry to half of it, and an exact Taylor-form theorem at the corner where the margin of the test vanishes. Lean's kernel checks the certificates with `decide +kernel`. The trusted base is Lean's kernel, including its built-in arithmetic on natural-number literals (GMP-accelerated), and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.
entries.title: The optimal Hessian bound for convex four-body central configurations

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no cited hypothesis, of Theorem 1.2 of A. Alsetri and X. Shao, Density versions of the binary Goldbach problem, arXiv 2405.18576v2, Acta Arith. 218, 2025, 285 to 295: if A is a set of primes whose relative lower density in every reduced residue class b mod W is at least some eta > 1/2, then almost all even positive integers are a sum of two primes from A. The entry also proves the paper's Theorem 1.1, that relative density 1 - epsilon in the primes alone does not suffice, and the sharpness of the constant 1/2 stated in its Remark 1.3. A derived result of this entry, not a result of the paper, shows that the hypothesis of Theorem 1.2 holds for the set of all primes, so the theorem is not vacuous. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; Theorem 1.2 concerns almost all even numbers. An AI agent wrote the Lean code, except the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd code credited to its authors; the statements were checked against the paper by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.
entries.title: A density version of the binary Goldbach problem, after Alsetri and Shao

entries.abstract: Formalization of the near-linear directed-cycle theorem: for every real epsilon greater than zero, all sufficiently large finite connected vertex-transitive loopless digraphs on n vertices contain a simple directed cycle of length at least n^(1-epsilon). Connectedness means connectedness of the underlying undirected graph; cycles of length two are allowed. This is Theorem 1.5 of the archived revised manuscript by Bowen Li and Abhishek Methuku, with repaired arguments and replacement lemmas in its proof dependencies. It does not assert Hamiltonicity.
entries.title: Nearly linear directed cycles in vertex-transitive digraphs

entries.abstract: Machine-checked proofs of conjectures recorded in 29 entries of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), together with corrections of the four conjectured statements that turn out to be false. Most of the sequences are coefficients of formal power series defined by functional equations, and most of the results describe their residues modulo small integers. The results form six families and a group of further results: the equation A(x*A - m*x*A^2) = x^2 (parity, residues modulo m^2, binary-digit divisibility and prime exponents for every m, with corrected residue classifications modulo 9 and 16 for A396843 and A396844); consecutive iterates F = x + F^{o r}*F^{o(r+1)} (every integer iterate modulo 2r, A396099, A396798, A396807); scaled inverses A(x - x*A(qx)/q) = x (every coefficient is 1 modulo q+1, and for even q the odd coefficients are exactly at the powers of 2, A393856-A393859); theta-series substitutions and theta-type sums (square patterns modulo 4, corrected for A380680, and a congruence modulo 16 for A355872); Catalan-type equations (residues modulo 2, 4 and 8 governed by powers of 2, A393172, A393171, A389536, A397588, A195194); equations with an exact halving step (residues modulo 4, 9 and 3, A389537, A389542, A389474, A389475); and further results on A396093, A392210, A396102 and its family F^{o r} = (1+x)*F^{o(r-1)}, A380056, A397346 and the greedy sequence A394576. Each family has its own Comparator configuration, and each OEIS entry has a self-contained paper in the repository.
entries.title: Proofs and corrections of OEIS conjectures
